gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a tracker's cycle predictions only use your body's signals if the device has a skin-temperature sensor. Garmin's Lily 2 Active has no such sensor (the5krunner lists 'Skin temperature: No'). Fitbit's fertile window 'adjusts based on the cycle data you enter'. Apple Watch SE 3 and Oura do measure temperature: Apple uses wrist temperature for retrospective ovulation estimates after about 5 nights, and both work with Natural Cycles, an app the FDA has cleared as birth control.
standout_why: The three cited rivals (womenshealthmag.com, goodhousekeeping.com, wired.com) and wearablebeat.com and tomsguide.com could not be opened: they returned blocked, 403 or truncated pages. So I could not confirm that none of them mentions temperature sensors. ChatGPT's answer, which those pages fed, gives the Lily 2 Active 'menstrual cycle tracking' and the Charge 6 'cycle logging' as if they were the same feature as Apple's 'cycle insights'. It never says which devices measure temperature or which ones work with Natural Cycles. Our current page also blurs this: it lists 'skin temperature' for the Inspire 3 and 'Cycle + pregnancy logging' for the Lily 2 Active.
decides: The finding splits the candidates into two groups. Some only log a calendar: the Garmin Lily 2 Active (no skin-temperature sensor) and Fitbit, whose fertile window comes from data you enter. Others read a temperature signal: Apple Watch SE 3, Oura Ring 4 and certain Garmin Venu/Forerunner models. A shopper who wants ovulation insight or temperature-based contraception should get the SE 3 (iPhone only) or the Oura Ring 4, not the Lily 2 Active. The Lily 2 Active is still the right pick for small wrists and step and workout tracking. The page should rename the 'Cycle tracking' column so it separates 'logs and predicts from your inputs' from 'reads skin temperature', and should drop or source the 'skin temperature' claim for the Inspire 3.

findings.label: Wrist-temperature models and how ovulation estimates work
findings.value: Apple lists 'An Apple Watch Series 8 or later, any model of Apple Watch Ultra, or Apple Watch SE 3'. 'your wrist temperature can also be used to provide retrospective ovulation estimates and improve period predictions'
findings.source_title: Apple Support: Wrist temperature on Apple Watch

findings.label: Requirement before temperature data appears
findings.value: About 5 nights to set a baseline. Sleep Focus must be on for at least 4 hours a night. 'While you sleep, Apple Watch samples your temperature every five seconds'
findings.source_title: Apple Support: Wrist temperature on Apple Watch
findings.note: The page also says 'If the fit is too loose, it can impact wrist temperature data'. Track Sleep with Apple Watch must be turned on. Not a medical device.

findings.label: Skin temperature sensor
findings.value: Skin temperature: No. Sensors: Elevate wrist HR, Pulse Ox, compass, accelerometer, ambient light
findings.note: Named reviewer's spec sheet. Garmin's US product page could not be opened (404 on the URLs tried). Battery figures on the same page: 9 days in smartwatch mode, 9 h with GPS.

findings.label: Natural Cycles (FDA-cleared birth control): compatible wearables
findings.value: NC° Band 1/2, NC° Ring, Oura Ring 2, 3, 4, 4 Ceramic and 5; Apple Watch Series 8 to 11, Ultra 1 to 3 and SE3; Garmin Venu, Forerunner, quatix, tactix, fēnix, Enduro and CIRQA models; WHOOP MG and 5.0. 'To be compatible, your Garmin wearable needs to have a temperature sensor'. 'Any other wearables are not intended to be used with Natural Cycles'
findings.source_title: Natural Cycles Help: Which wearables are compatible with Natural Cycles
findings.note: Fitbit is not on the list. The page says not to manually log temperature data taken from Fitbit. The Garmin Lily line is not among the Garmin families listed.

findings.label: Natural Cycles pairing and FDA status
findings.value: 'Natural Cycles can be used with any Oura Ring model (Gen 2 and later)'. 'Natural Cycles is FDA-cleared to be used as a birth control method and fertility tracker'
findings.note: Requires both a Natural Cycles subscription and an Oura Membership.

findings.label: How Fitbit/Google Health sets the fertile window
findings.value: 'Your estimated fertile window automatically adjusts based on the cycle data you enter'. Trends need at least 3 completed cycles and use the last 6 months of data. A logged positive ovulation test moves the ovulation day.
findings.source_title: Google Health / Fitbit Help: Track your menstrual cycle
findings.note: The article does not mention skin temperature as an input. It says period logging on the device is available on Sense 2, Versa 2 and Pixel Watch 3/4. The Inspire 3 is not named.
